messages:
Amir: quick thread for a narrow follow-up  thinking about a lightweight prewarm "escrow" approach for dedicated GPU pools. goal: let tenants request short-lived prewarm capacity without blowing headroom or complicating billing. sketch below and questions.

Amir: TL;DR: tenant requests an escrow -> controller stamps a tokenized lease (ttl ms) -> runtime attempts warmup (kv cache + model load) -> if request materializes, token used; else token expires and is reconciled. wants: clear accounting, eviction-safe warmups.

Amir: proto config: ```prewarm:
  mode: escrow
  ttl_ms: 90000
  max_concurrent_per_tenant: 2
  global_ephemeral_cap: 120
  billing: meter-only-if-consumed
  eviction_behavior: shield_for_ms: 5000
```

Zoe: Love the tokenized lease idea. How do we prevent tenants from gaming with many tiny escrows? we should rate-limit by tenant QPS + a small credit burn on request.

Amir: agreed. proposal: a micro-charge (observability credit) on every escrow request that resets on consumption. charge is negligible but discourages spammers. recorded as usage but not invoiced unless consumed.

Vivian: eviction/shielding nuance: runtime can honor `shield_for_ms` but if node is under critical pressure we need a deterministic eviction precedence list. warmup=true leases should be below SLA-reserved tokens but above noop background tasks. also keep a metric `shield_evictions` to catch abuse.

Sam: curious about billing reconciliation. we have three counters: reserved_tokens, ephemeral_consumed_tokens, ephemeral_requested_tokens. Billing should only invoice reserved + ephemeral_consumed. Controllers need idempotent reconciliation windows to avoid double-billing across retries.

Amir: yes  add a reconciliation job that collapses lease events into a single consumption event per-tenant-per-request idempotently. store lease_id -> final_state.

Zoe: ops question: if an escrow expires during warmup (race), we must surface a `warmup_race` event for debugging. small note: track `warmup_waste_ms` and `kv_fill_progress_pct` so we can tune thresholds.

orch-bot: canary-rollout-job 77222 queued (canary-tenants: 50, trace: mixed-burst-week). ETA ~6h.

Vivian: also consider a hybrid policy: predictive lookahead allocates soft headroom based on model, while escrow handles sudden microbursts. If both claim capacity we prefer predictive for billing clarity. implement simple tie-breaker: predictive > escrow > shared-burst.

Amir: simulation plan: replay 30 days of traces with churn + sudden tenant migrations. compare metrics: 99p latency, cost-per-token, wasted-warmup-seconds, shield_evictions. run sweeping values for ttl_ms: [30k, 60k, 90k] and shield_for_ms: [2k,5k,10k].

Sam: add a safety cutoff: if global_ephemeral_cap < 10% of pool, disable escrows and fall back to predictive-only, to prevent cascading failures.

Zoe: API surface we want exposed: `POST /v1/premiums/escrow {tenant_id, purpose, ttl_ms}` -> returns `lease_id` and `status:{granted, queued, denied}`; `POST /v1/premiums/escrow/{lease_id}/consume` -> mark consumed. `DELETE /v1/premiums/escrow/{lease_id}` -> release. keep idempotency keys.

Amir: perfect. i'll capture this in a short RFC + simulation results once job finishes. thanks all.

Zoe: quick +1. excited to see the sims. :rocket:
